statement: The sum of two even natural numbers is even.
The square root of 2 is irrational.
For every natural number n there is a prime number p with p at least n.
For natural numbers a and b, the greatest common divisor of a and b divides a.
Addition of natural numbers is commutative.
Every natural number n is less than 2 to the power n.
Fermat's little theorem: for a prime p and an element a of the integers modulo p, a to the power p equals a.
Twice the sum of the natural numbers below n equals n times (n minus 1).
The square of a real number is nonnegative.
The absolute value of a real number is nonnegative.
Cauchy-Schwarz: in a real inner product space the absolute value of the inner product of x and y is at most the norm of x times the norm of y.
Weighted arithmetic-geometric mean inequality for two nonnegative reals: z1 to the power w1 times z2 to the power w2 is at most w1 z1 plus w2 z2 when w1 plus w2 equals 1.
Lagrange's theorem: the order of a subgroup of a finite group divides the order of the group.
Cauchy's theorem: if a prime p divides the order of a finite group G, then G has an element of order p.
Every group whose order is a prime number is cyclic.
Intermediate value theorem: a continuous real function on a closed interval [a, b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b).
A continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact set attains its maximum.
Rolle's theorem: if f is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b) and f(a) equals f(b), then the derivative of f vanishes at some point of (a, b).
The derivative of x to the power n is n times x to the power n minus 1.
Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a convergent subsequence.
For a real r with 0 at most r and r less than 1, the sum of r to the power n over all natural numbers n equals 1 divided by (1 minus r).
The harmonic series, the sum of 1/n over the positive integers, is not summable.
The sum of 1/n squared over the positive integers equals pi squared over 6.
Binomial theorem: in a commutative semiring (x + y) to the power n equals the sum over k of x to the k times y to the (n - k) times n choose k.
Pigeonhole principle: a function from a finite set to a smaller finite set takes the same value at two distinct points.
Wilson's theorem: for a prime p, (p - 1) factorial is congruent to -1 modulo p.
Lagrange's four-square theorem: every natural number is a sum of four squares.
Fermat's two-square theorem: a prime congruent to 1 modulo 4 is a sum of two squares of natural numbers.
Chinese remainder theorem: for coprime natural numbers m and n and any a and b there is a natural number congruent to a modulo m and to b modulo n.
Cantor's theorem: there is no surjection from a set onto its power set.
